title: Bad-locus contradiction for affine limit fibre dimensions
statement: With the same directed finite-type affine system and surjective comparison maps as in lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound, if every stage has a prime whose fibre dimension is strictly greater than d, then the limiting fibre has dimension strictly greater than d; equivalently, the stagewise bad-prime hypothesis contradicts the bound on every limiting fibre.

source.place: Tag 05M5, affine specialization, bad-locus construction and Noetherian fibre stabilization

proof.text: For each i let Z_i be the complement of the open locus where the local dimension of the fibre of Spec C_i → Spec A_i is at most d. Openness is the scheme-level bounded-local-fibre-dimension theorem. The supremum of local dimensions and the canonical identification of the affine residue-field pullback with the scheme fibre show that the bad-prime hypothesis makes every Z_i nonempty. A closed immersion embeds each later fibre in the base change of the earlier fibre. Local dimension decreases under an embedding and is invariant under the finite-type base change, so transition maps carry Z_j into Z_i. Apply Mathlib exists_mem_of_isClosed_of_nonempty to Spec of the colimit cocone to obtain x whose projections belong to every Z_i.

Put s=f(x), K=κ(s), and B_i=C_i ⨿_{A_i} K. Construct their transition maps by the pushout universal property and a colimit cocone with vertex B=(colimit C) ⨿_{colimit A} K. For any cocone the restrictions of its maps to K agree at a common upper bound, and its restrictions to C_i descend uniquely through colimit C. These two descended maps agree on colimit A and determine the unique map out of B. Pushout pasting expresses B_i → B_j as a base change of the given surjective comparison map, hence it is surjective.

Fix i. The ring B_i is finite type over the field K and hence Noetherian. Choose finitely many generators of the kernel B_i → B. Each generator dies at a finite stage by the elementwise filtered-colimit equality criterion. A cocone over the finite family of killing maps gives a single index j killing all generators. Every B_i → B_j and every B_j → B is surjective: a representative at an arbitrary stage can be lifted after passing to a common upper bound. If two elements of B_j have equal images in B, lift them to B_i; their difference lies in the finitely generated kernel and thus is killed in B_j. Therefore B_j → B is bijective.

The point x has a canonical fibre point in X_s, identified by the pushout square with a point y of Spec B. Transport y along the isomorphism B_j → B. Its image in Spec C_j is x_j by the explicit cocone equations. The base-change dimension theorem and the fact that the fibre of a K-scheme over its unique base point is isomorphic to that scheme identify the local dimension there with the local fibre dimension at x_j. Since x_j belongs to Z_j this exceeds d. But the local dimension at y is at most the dimension of the whole limiting fibre, which the hypothesis bounds by d. Contradiction.
